set_title: Spondylo- names: wear, break, slip, inflammation or infection of the vertebrae
stem: A 15-year-old girl who trains in gymnastics 20 hours a week has had low back pain for 2 months. The pain worsens when she arches her back and eases with rest. She has no fever, and strength, reflexes and sensation in her legs are normal. No step-off is felt along the spine. An oblique x-ray of the lumbar spine shows a lucent line across the pars interarticularis of L5, and a lateral view shows normal alignment.
oneliner: 15F gymnast + low back pain worse on arching + lucent line across the L5 pars, normal alignment → ?

whyNot.A: Spondylosis is age-related wear with osteophytes in older adults; she is **15 with a lucent line across the pars**
whyNot.C: Ankylosing spondylitis causes inflammatory pain that improves with exercise; her pain is **worse when she arches her back and better with rest**
whyNot.D: Spondylolisthesis means the vertebra has slipped forward; her lateral view shows **normal alignment with no step-off**
whyNot.E: Spondylodiscitis is an infection with fever and a damaged disc; she has **no fever and a lucent line through the pars, not the disc**

why: spondylo = vertebra and -lysis = loosening, here a break: a stress fracture of the pars interarticularis with no slip. **An adolescent gymnast with back pain on extension and a pars lucency but normal alignment** has spondylolysis. On the oblique x-ray the defect looks like a collar on the neck of the "Scottie dog".

rows: Spondylosis
spondyl = vertebra; -osis = condition (wear)
Age-related wear of the discs and facet joints with bone spurs: osteoarthritis of the spine
Older adult with long-standing neck or low back pain and stiffness
**Narrowed disc spaces and osteophytes on x-ray**
Spondylolysis
spondylo = vertebra; -lysis = loosening, a break
Stress fracture of the pars interarticularis, usually at L5, with no slip
Adolescent athlete who arches the back again and again (gymnast, diver, lineman)
**Pain on back extension; a "collar" across the Scottie dog's neck on an oblique x-ray**
Spondylolisthesis
spondylo = vertebra; -listhesis = slipping
Forward slip of one vertebra on the one below, often L5 on S1
Adolescent with bilateral pars fractures, or an older adult with degeneration at L4-L5
**Palpable step-off of the spinous processes; tight hamstrings**
Ankylosing spondylitis
ankylosing = stiffening into fusion; spondyl = vertebra; -itis = inflammation
HLA-B27-associated inflammation of the sacroiliac joints, spine and entheses that ends in fusion
Young man with back pain and morning stiffness that improve with exercise and worsen with rest
**Bilateral sacroiliitis, reduced chest expansion, anterior uveitis; bamboo spine late**
Spondylodiscitis
spondylo = vertebra; disc; -itis = inflammation (here infection)
Infection of a disc and the two vertebral bodies on either side of it
Injection drug use, bacteremia or a recent spine procedure; Staphylococcus aureus most often; tuberculosis (Pott disease)
**Fever, focal spinal tenderness, high ESR; MRI shows the disc and both endplates involved**
Cervical spondylotic myelopathy
spondylotic = from spondylosis; myelo = spinal cord; -pathy = disease
Compression of the cervical spinal cord by degenerative spurs, disc bulge and thick ligaments
Older adult with clumsy hands and an unsteady gait
**Upper motor neuron signs: hyperreflexia, Hoffmann sign, spastic gait**

idea.rule: Spondylolysis = the pars is broken but the vertebra stays in place; once it slides forward it is spondylolisthesis.
also: Repeated hyperextension (gymnastics, diving, football lineman) stresses the pars, most often at L5
Bilateral defects can progress to spondylolisthesis
Most heal with rest from the sport, a brace and physical therapy

set_title: Spondylo- names: wear, break, slip, inflammation or infection of the vertebrae
stem: A 16-year-old boy who plays as a lineman in football has had low back pain and tight hamstrings for 6 months. Bending forward is limited, and a step-off is felt over the lower lumbar spinous processes. He has no fever or morning stiffness. A lateral x-ray shows the L5 vertebral body displaced forward on S1 by about one quarter of its width.
oneliner: 16M lineman + back pain, tight hamstrings, palpable step-off + L5 shifted forward on S1 → ?

whyNot.A: Spondylodiscitis is a spine infection with fever and endplate destruction; he has **no fever and a forward shift of L5 on S1**
whyNot.B: Ankylosing spondylitis causes inflammatory back pain with long morning stiffness; he has **no morning stiffness and a palpable step-off**
whyNot.C: Spondylolysis is a pars fracture with normal alignment; his x-ray shows **L5 displaced forward on S1**
whyNot.E: Spondylosis is degenerative wear with osteophytes in older adults; he is **16 with a vertebra that has slipped**

why: spondylo = vertebra and -listhesis = slipping: one vertebra slides forward on the one below. **A step-off over the lumbar spine with L5 displaced forward on S1** is spondylolisthesis. In adolescents it usually follows bilateral pars fractures; in older adults it comes from facet and disc wear at L4-L5.

set_title: Spondylo- names: wear, break, slip, inflammation or infection of the vertebrae
stem: A 24-year-old man has had low back and buttock pain for 8 months, with morning stiffness that lasts over an hour. The pain wakes him in the second half of the night, improves with exercise, and worsens with rest. Forward bending of the lumbar spine and chest expansion are reduced. Last year he had a painful red eye with sensitivity to light. Pelvic x-rays show erosions and sclerosis of both sacroiliac joints.
oneliner: 24M + 8 months of back pain with long morning stiffness, better with exercise + reduced chest expansion + red eye + bilateral sacroiliitis → ?

whyNot.A: Spondylosis is mechanical wear in older adults that worsens with use; he is **24 with stiffness that eases with exercise**
whyNot.B: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy compresses the neck cord with hand clumsiness and brisk reflexes; he has **low back pain with erosions of both sacroiliac joints**
whyNot.C: Spondylodiscitis is an infection with fever and one painful level; he has **8 months of stiffness, a red eye and bilateral sacroiliitis**
whyNot.D: Spondylolysis is a pars fracture with pain on extension; his pain **improves with exercise and worsens with rest, with sacroiliac erosions**

why: ankylosing = stiffening into fusion, spondyl = vertebra, -itis = inflammation: the spine is inflamed and slowly fuses. **A young man with back pain and long morning stiffness that eases with exercise, reduced chest expansion, past uveitis and bilateral sacroiliitis** has ankylosing spondylitis. It is an HLA-B27-associated spondyloarthritis that inflames entheses.

set_title: Spondylo- names: wear, break, slip, inflammation or infection of the vertebrae
stem: A 68-year-old woman has had neck pain and stiffness for several years that worsens toward the end of the day and with prolonged reading. She has no fever, weight loss, hand clumsiness or trouble walking. Strength, reflexes, sensation and gait are normal. A cervical spine x-ray shows narrowed disc spaces at C5-C6 and C6-C7 with osteophytes at the vertebral margins, and alignment is normal.
oneliner: 68F + years of neck pain worse by evening + normal neuro exam + narrowed discs with osteophytes → ?

whyNot.B: Spondylolisthesis means a vertebra has slipped forward; her x-ray shows **normal alignment**
whyNot.C: Ankylosing spondylitis begins in young adults with stiffness that eases with activity; she is **68 with pain that worsens with use through the day**
whyNot.D: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy adds cord compression with clumsy hands and brisk reflexes; she has **no hand clumsiness, normal reflexes and a normal gait**
whyNot.E: Spondylolysis is a pars stress fracture in young athletes; she is **68 with narrowed discs and osteophytes**

why: spondyl = vertebra and -osis = a condition, here wear: osteoarthritis of the spine. **An older adult with years of mechanical neck pain, narrowed disc spaces and osteophytes, and a normal neurologic exam** has spondylosis. If the spurs press on a root it causes radiculopathy, and if they press on the cord it becomes cervical spondylotic myelopathy.
